newsitem.title: UK: Energis poised to connect with Europe player.
newsitem.headline: Energis poised to connect with Europe player.

text.p: British telecoms company Energis, which is wholly-owned by the National Grid, said on Friday it was poised to announce its first continental deal in a move that will help slash the cost of European business telephone calls.

With an international licence safely under its belt, Energis said it was looking to spark an aggressive price war on European business telephone routes with an "imminent" new correspondent agreement with a major telecom player.
Chief executive Mike Grabiner told Reuters in an interview that the company was "close to closing deals with a number of European operators".
"We will be announcing our next agreement in the next few weeks," he said, adding that European business telephone prices were due to come down "quite dramatically".
Energis has already signed a correspondent agreement with Sprint, America's third international carrier, to end each other's transatlantic calls.
The British government last month broke a duopoly between British Telecommunications and Mercury on owning international calls networks last month, awarding 44 new international licences.
Rivals such as Energis, which used to have to lease line capacity from BT and Mercury at high prices, can now buy permanent line capacity from others -- and save a lot of money.
"We have a very small market share, a dramatically reduced cost base and every incentive to be aggressive on price to grow our market share. And we will do that," Grabiner said.
Energis, which supplies telecoms services to 13,000-14,000 business customers, says European telephone prices are likely to fall by at least 20 percent -- and could fall much further.
Last October, the company offered to undercut BT by about 50 percent with a 10 pence-per-minute charge for selected business customers on direct dialled calls to America.

Grabiner said: "European prices have further to go than North American prices...The key thing is having a relationship in place with (partners such as) France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom, in the short term."

Energis was set up in 1993 and operates one of the country's most advanced networks by wrapping 4,500 kms of fibre optic cables -- capable of transmitting images and data as well as voice -- around the earthwires between overhead power pylons.
